definitions.explanation: The son of one's brother or sister. The 〜っ{子|こ} ending adds warmth and is the form most people use in conversation, especially when the nephew is still a child.

examples.japanese: {甥|おい}っ{子|こ}が{生|う}まれた。
{甥|おい}っ{子|こ}に{誕生日|たんじょうび}のプレゼントを{送|おく}った。
examples.english: I sent my nephew a birthday present.

examples.japanese: {正月|しょうがつ}に{甥|おい}っ{子|こ}が{遊|あそ}びに{来|き}て、{家|いえ}の{中|なか}がにぎやかになった。
examples.english: My nephew came to visit at New Year's and the house got lively.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {甥|おい}っ{子|こ}が{生|う}まれる: to have a nephew born
- {甥|おい}っ{子|こ}の{面倒|めんどう}を{見|み}る: to look after one's nephew
- {甥|おい}っ{子|こ}にお{年玉|としだま}をあげる: to give one's nephew New Year's money

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {甥|おい}: nephew — the plain term; used in writing and formal speech, where {甥|おい}っ{子|こ} would sound too cosy
- {姪|めい}っ{子|こ}: niece — the matching form
- {孫|まご}: grandchild — often mentioned alongside when talking about the younger generation

The same 〜っ{子|こ} pattern appears in words like {江戸|えど}っ{子|こ} (a born-and-bred Tokyoite), where it likewise marks familiarity rather than small size.
